<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD for lcms2-cmake appears to be standard packaging code with no evidence of malicious injection. The source is fetched from the expected upstream GitHub repository (mm2/Little-CMS), a b2sum checksum is provided (not SKIP), and the build/package functions follow conventional patterns (cmake build, make install, removal of unnecessary files, license installation). The only notable oddity is the maintainer email obfuscated via base64 encoding in the metadata field, but this is merely a privacy/hygiene choice for contact info and is never executed as code. No suspicious network requests, eval/base64-assembled commands, backdoors, or data exfiltration patterns are present.
</details>

There are no executable scripts, network calls, or code execution within this file. No suspicious patterns such as obfuscated payloads, unexpected file operations, or dangerous commands are present.

- Only metadata keys (`pkgbase`, `pkgdesc`, `source`, `b2sums`, etc.) are defined.
- The `source` field references the upstream tarball `https://github.com/mm2/Little-CMS/archive/lcms2.19.1.tar.gz`, which is a legitimate, public source.
- A checksum (`b2sums`) is provided for integrity verification.
- No scripting languages, network downloads, or system modifications appear in the file.

The file adheres to normal AUR packaging practices and poses no security risk.
</details>
